W2 (empirical), after E037. Tip is still E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. That is E035 plus a whitening-bias stop at 20% of steps. The margin over the 0.753 gate is about zero. Held-out seeds ran about 0.2 pp below seeds 0-2 in earlier tips, so the population mean is probably near 0.751-0.752. The official 0.75 bar is at risk.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 added a freeze plus 0.5 epoch and gave -0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. Time-neutral boosters failed 7 times in a row (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS, and others). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within noise (about ±0.2 pp).
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28 and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation on memory-bound large maps is the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 moved the freeze from 75% to 60% of steps. It saved 0.25 s (-4.6%) but cost 0.38 pp, about 0.65 s per pp. That is better than the epoch dial in time per pp, but it still failed the 0.753 gate. The returns are now at or below the break-even rate against an epoch top-up, so the stem trims are near exhausted.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims and freezes, since the savings were larger than modelled. I was too optimistic on time-neutral accuracy gains. Accuracy ranges mostly held, except where the change cut training signal (E030, E032, E037).

Unsure: how much margin remains on held-out seeds. Further trims need an accuracy refund, and that refund costs epochs. The tip is probably near the Pareto front for this architecture. The effect of replacing Muon with SGD is uncertain, and E006 suggests losing Muon costs accuracy. I can't judge the PCIe transfer of the bandwidth-bound levers, because it was never measured here.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic, no recipe change. Time is unchanged. Fresh seeds likely land near 0.752, below the 0.753 gate, with winner's-curse shrinkage.
BN folding saves a little on the frozen stem. Group 1 backward is already gone, so the saving is perhaps 1-2%. The accuracy shift comes from running stats, which are mostly noise.
Profiling only, with no recipe change. Non-GEMM kernels are likely at least 30% of the step, as the E028 saving suggests.
SGD drops the Newton-Schulz overhead for about 3% less time. E006 and the SGD recipe suggest a loss of about 0.3-0.5 pp, so it likely fails the gate.

cruxes: What is the true population mean of the tip on fresh seeds? If it is below 0.752, every further trim needs an epoch refund, and the time gains stop.
Does replacing Muon with SGD cost more than 0.3 pp? That decides whether the roughly 3% Newton-Schulz time is available.
How much of the frozen-stem step is BN or elementwise traffic that BN folding can remove? That sets the value of I057.
